doc.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Growing up in Fyzabad, dancing, and the broken neck at sixteen
summary: He grew up in a folk culture in Fyzabad, hearing shango drums, danced from age five until a car accident ended it, and describes his brothers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Absolutely. Absolutely. Well I started, you know as I mentioned, I am from Trinidad. And I grew up in a folk culture. I was first a dancer. I started dancing at age five and went through until I was about fifteen, sixteen years old, dancing. All my life I was close to the drum. I remember where we lived in Fyzabad, which is deep south Trinidad. A lot of roots, a lot of culture. There was a shango yard not too far away up on the hill, and I used to hear the drums coming across at night when I was you know, about to go to sleep. And they were in ceremony and everything. I remember this having a very, very profound effect on my psyche much later on of course. Because you’re up at night and you’re hearing these drums. And then you go and you’re performing and you’re dancing and stuff and you’re part of the tradition and part of this, and this is what you’re dancing. You know you’re dancing to shango, you’re dancing the Trinidad folk culture, you’re dancing pique, and bellaire and bongo and joropo and all kinds of stuff that was going on. And so much later on, much later on, when I was not dancing anymore, that energy had to find a way out and it just went to the music. And at sixteen years old it stopped for me. I had a really bad accident. I broke my neck, I was hit by a car, by a van, and broke my neck. So my dance, my aspirations for a dance life ended. It wasn’t a final thing but the level of performance for me at that point in time, I just was not able to keep, so I moved on, and that energy came out in the music. I dedicated myself to the music. And all throughout university, all throughout my other jobs and everything else, when I finished university, it was at university that I actually started to take the music to a whole other level because I was the first of my family to go abroad to study. I have three brothers, I’m the second. My oldest brother is all art and music. Me: I am a cross between the art and the sciences. At least that’s how I live my life. The brother after me was physics and the baby of the family got his Ph.D. at 27 years old and he leads the field today in genetic material that causes epilepsy in human beings, right?
